title: Say her name in a bright, happy voice
note: Used by two steps. The empty hands are load-bearing: paying is step 4, so a treat visible here collapses two steps and teaches luring instead of a voluntary check-in. Round 3 did not fail on a treat — it failed on occlusion: only one hand was in frame, the other lost behind the near thigh on the pouch side, which leaves the viewer unable to tell. A crouch hides a hand that a stand does not, so each hand is now placed by name rather than described as a pair. Round 3 also sat the handler's eyes above Lucy's, so the eye line is stated as a comparison rather than as 'at her level'. The eye-line claim was removed from mustBeTrue after round 4 shipped. Rounds 2, 3 and 4 all drew the handler's head above Lucy's, through three different phrasings including an explicit head-top comparison, so the sentence is not the lever — the post-mortems say the attachment is, and no redrawn scene yet shows a handler crouched to a seated dog's eye line to attach as one. The scene text still asks for it; mustBeTrue no longer claims it, because a review question the shipped picture fails is a false pass on every future round. Restore the claim when there is a reference that can carry it.
scene: Interior entry hall, beside the closed charcoal front door. The handler crouches down beside Lucy, knees bent, back straight, her face turned toward Lucy — she does not lean over the dog or reach across her. She is down far enough that her eyes are level with Lucy's eyes: the top of her head must not sit higher than the top of Lucy's head. Lucy has turned away from the door and looks up at the handler's face, ears soft and attentive, sitting square. Both of the handler's hands are drawn in full, and both are completely empty — no treat, no food, nothing in either hand. Place them so that neither one can be hidden: the near hand rests open on top of her near knee, palm down, fingers relaxed and separated; the far hand rests open on her far thigh, forward of the knee and clearly in front of her body. Neither hand is tucked behind a leg, behind her back, or outside the frame, and neither is reaching toward Lucy. Both hands stay well clear of the mustard treat pouch, with open space visible between the nearer hand and the pouch. The black leash is still clipped to the ring on Lucy's collar and still runs down slack under the handler's near shoe. Since Lucy is black and the leash is black, draw the leash with a thin lighter outline where it passes near her body so the line stays readable against her coat; it must not cross her back or shoulders. Background: the door, the doormat, one baseboard line. Nothing else.
mustBeTrue: both of the handler's hands are fully drawn, visibly empty and clear of the pouch with neither hidden behind a leg, Lucy is looking at the handler's face and not at the door, the handler is crouched beside Lucy rather than leaning over her, and the room matches the continuity reference.
